scope: Curated static source evidence across the parent and exact pinned runtime dependencies, with mandatory P001 category and launch-stage coverage. Not an exhaustive API census or runtime qualification.
excerpt_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact UTF-8 source bytes for the inclusive 1-based line range, preserving original line endings.

evidence.explanation: The target generator selects x86_64 and i386 Darwin triplets. This source does not define an ARM target or ARM-to-x86 translation engine.
FAT slice selection handles x86_64/i386 and explicitly fails the aarch64 compilation path. ARM-related constants elsewhere do not establish executable ARM support.
The main loader has a second explicit aarch64 barrier at stack setup.
CMake builds the native darling command and requests setuid installation. Source inspection does not prove those privileges are available on a particular test host.
The native launcher creates namespaces, forks, and executes darlingserver with prefix/user/group/synchronization arguments.
mldr is a host executable linked to native loader libraries and generated darlingserver RPC wrappers; it is distinct from the Mach-O images it loads.
The loader maps Mach-O segments through Linux mappings. This is real implementation code, but its validation and compatibility correctness are not qualified in P001.
LC_LOAD_DYLINKER resolves a linker path and recursively loads that Mach-O dynamic linker. The child dyld implementation belongs to a separate pinned submodule.
mldr creates its RPC socket and process-lifetime pipe and checks in with darlingserver. Errors terminate startup; these paths were inspected, not executed.
After stack preparation, mldr reports executable and dyld image metadata to the server before transferring control.
The startup stack carries an elf_calls table pointer in its Apple-style auxiliary string vector. This provides a source-backed host/guest boundary, not CPU translation.
The native helper table exposes ELF loading, allocation/thread services, and server socket access to the Darling runtime.
The x86_64 path installs the prepared stack pointer and jumps to the loaded entry point. No executed guest result is claimed.
The core build composes kernel/syscall compatibility, dyld, libSystem, Objective-C, and CoreFoundation from their source owners. Build order is not runtime initializer order.

It moved eight more lines due solely to the exact libxpc lifecycle bridge added above; the original four-line movement from static-unwind and Objective-C adapters remains separately reviewed. The opt-in probes do not establish framework completeness.

evidence.explanation: Build policy separates GUI implementation sources from the broad stub group; individual implementation bodies still require inspection and behavioral tests.
Development link stubs are a separate packaging path; when GUI is selected, the source requests NO_INSTALL for these competing stubs.
This AudioToolbox target intentionally builds the developer stub source, not the separate src/CoreAudio implementation.
Representative developer AudioToolbox exports have generic pointer-returning, null-returning placeholder bodies.
The checked-in C-function generator emits generic void* functions that return NULL. This proves generator behavior; it does not establish the historical generator used for every stub file.
The inspected CoreMIDI exports are generic placeholder bodies. A symbol or null/success value is not evidence of MIDI client lifecycle implementation.
The selected vDSP transform exports are placeholder bodies and provide no numerical output behavior.
vDSP also contains a nontrivial loop implementation. This classification means non-stub code exists, not that the scalar/stride semantics or boundary behavior are correct.
AudioComponentManager contains bundle/factory lookup, instance construction, and Open invocation with error paths. Full lifecycle and failure correctness are unqualified.
Synchronous instantiation dispatch exists, while asynchronous AudioComponentInstantiate only logs and does not invoke its completion handler.
The validator assigns Passed unconditionally. Its return value cannot qualify an Audio Unit.
The host time API returns a constant zero; source inspection establishes a placeholder, not a working audio clock.
Bytes-per-frame calculation includes sample rate, exposing a dimensional error in the default format setup. P001 records the defect without claiming a repair.
IOSurface has Objective-C forwarding paths alongside a zero-returning XPC-object creation placeholder; the whole framework cannot be classified as implemented.
Several ImageIO entry points forward into Onyx2D implementation objects. This confirms source integration, not codec coverage, ownership correctness, or rendering results.
An adjacent ImageIO data-provider constructor is a stub, so the framework is partial despite its real forwarding functions.

The historical P001 citation retains exact original relative URLs at the audited commit. The P002 re-audit independently pins the current URL-only rewrite and checks that all non-URL source bytes, source ownership and 149 dependency targets are unchanged.
The build recommends Clang11, enforces an out-of-source directory, and rejects an i386/i686 host. This guard alone does not prove other host architectures work.

evidence.explanation: The actual loader target includes the dyld2 and ImageLoader bodies inspected below.
The main executable enters ImageLoader linking with the launch binding mode.
Linking loads the dependency graph then rebases and binds images subject to main-executable handling.
Inserted roots and the main executable dependency graph enter initializer processing.
The recursive initializer algorithm visits lower dependencies first, postpones upward dependencies, notifies Objective-C and then initializes the image.
Module initializer invocation guards the libSystem initialization boundary and observes installation of libSystem helpers.
Mach-O image initialization invokes the -init routine and module initializer functions.
dyld dispatches the registered Objective-C image initializer callback at the dependents-initialized state.
After initializer processing, dyld selects LC_MAIN with libdyld glue or the legacy LC_UNIXTHREAD entry. This is static control-flow evidence.
The libSystem.B.dylib target includes init.c.
The selected libSystem source declares the constructor entry.
The source orders kernel/platform/pthread/libc/malloc/dyld/dispatch/XPC initialization with the shown platform guards.
Server bootstrap launches mldr/vchroot with the configured init process and socket/root-path environment.
The RPC decoder validates call numbers and registers the process using check-in lifetime-pipe information.
RPC call construction checks typed message size and queues managed calls or schedules unmanaged processing.
The check-in implementation notifies process state and returns ESRCH if process/thread ownership is absent.
The pinned dispatch configuration enables Objective-C support.
The internal configuration selects the Objective-C object path from HAVE_OBJC.
The actual dispatch target includes queue initialization and the Objective-C object implementation.
libdispatch_init reaches object bootstrap after dispatch queue and timing setup.
The selected dispatch object initializer calls _objc_init and installs retain/release block callbacks.
Objective-C bootstraps its state and registers map/load/unmap image callbacks with dyld.
The dyld load-images callback discovers and invokes Objective-C +load methods under the shown locking boundaries.
Darling selects the MacOSX CoreFoundation branch, so a Linux-only constructor attribute cannot establish the actual initialization wiring.
The framework explicitly links __CFInitialize as its Mach-O -init routine.
CoreFoundation initialization guards reentry and records its main thread.
The framework initializer registers CoreFoundation types and their Objective-C bridge classes.
The initializer creates empty collection instances and marks initialization complete.
